lastCommit.message:
[ota-hal] OTA-1645 (slice 4b): the shield's AC is real

Seven shields print "+N AC" on the card. Not one point of it has ever
reached the number an enemy rolls against.

Measured before a line was written. A probe equipping the Titan Shield
— "+4 AC", 8 defense, the priciest shield in the game — read
`standingAc = 10`, identical to an empty off-hand, while a chest piece in
the control read 13. The cause is structural rather than arithmetic:
`equippedGearAc` walks ARMOR_SLOTS (head / chest / hands / legs / feet /
cloak) and a shield is a WEAPON that equips to a hand, so no AC reader in
the game has ever had one in view.

What the shields DID have is a `defense` number feeding the BLOCK roll and
a `statBonuses` HP grant, both live and both working. That is why this
survived so long: a shield was doing two of the three things on its card,
so it read as underwhelming rather than broken.

The term goes in `equippedGearAc` and NOWHERE else, because
`aggregateArmor` (the resolver's source) and `standingAc` (the sheet's)
both call it. That is the whole point of OTA-1133/1135 — one answer,
everywhere — and adding a shield term at either call site would put the
panel and the fight back out of step, which is the defect those two OTAs
were written to end. The DEFENCE card gains its own `shield +N` chip
beside armour and accessories, and the item card says "AC +4 while held".

  • Five unconditional shields now pay what they print: Bone Round +2,
    Giant Bone +3, Titan +4, Mud Royal +3, Mud Emperor's Buckler +3.
  • The two TYPED ones are carried apart in `shieldAc.vs` and spent at the
    resolver — the only line that knows the incoming damage type. Mud
    Heater "+2 AC vs fire" answers burn; Aetheric Shield "+2 AC vs energy"
    answers aetheric / electrical / burn, which is what its own
    description ("Deflects energy attacks") means. Deliberately outside
    `trimStandingAc`: the trim exists to stop a fully-fused STANDING build
    becoming untouchable, and cover that applies to one damage type in a
    fight you did not choose is not standing AC.
  • ⚠ The Aetheric Shield-Hammer's "+2 AC FOR 1 ROUND after a hit" is
    REFUSED by the parser. A timed status is not a held passive, and
    reading it here would hand a two-handed hammer a permanent +2 it never
    promised. ota1645 pins that refusal by name; it waits for 4c.

Three test repoints, all of them guards firing correctly rather than
noise, and each updated to follow the change rather than be loosened:

  • ota1135 pins the SOURCE TEXT of `aggregateArmor` and `standingAc` to
    prove neither re-derives AC. Both sums gained `+ gear.shield`, so the
    pins name the new sums — the assertion is that every term is read off
    the one helper, and a term computed locally would still break them.
  • ota1135's empty-player shape now expects the third component at zero.
  • ota1094's `catalogWeapons` fixture needed a `tags?: string[]` field
    and one explicit param type. ⚠ Those two typecheck errors were mine
    from OTA-1644: I edited that suite in response to a jest failure AFTER
    running the gates, and pushed without re-gating. The ratchet caught it
    here (203 > baseline 201) rather than in CI. Re-gated clean.

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green — 1108 suites /
11401 tests, 0 failures.
